back: Concentrating on producing a limited range of goods, services or tasks instead of producing everything.
Breaking a production process into separate tasks, each done by a different worker or group of workers.

front: Advantages of the division of labour
back: Skill and speed through repetition, less time wasted, shorter training, use of specialised machinery, higher output, lower unit costs and prices.

front: Disadvantages of the division of labour
back: Boredom, loss of craft skill, narrow skills (low occupational mobility), risk of replacement by machines, interdependence, standardised products.

front: What limits the division of labour?
back: The size of the market, the nature of the product and the capital available.
Relying on others because each worker, firm or country produces only part of what is needed; one stoppage can halt the whole process.
Home: cooking, cleaning, fetching water shared out. School: subject teachers, bursar. Industry: assembly lines, bakeries, clothing workshops.

front: Why does the division of labour lower cost per unit?
back: Output per worker rises, so the same wage bill is spread over more units.
